title: Where the Overdue Clock Starts on a Crop Input Purchasing Account
content:
The overdue days a service charge is worked over run from the last thing that moved on the account rather than from the day the account first went past due, where the record shows such a movement.

**Clause.** Where a service charge already stands assessed on the account over the 10 statement months before the handling date, the overdue days are counted from the day the most recent of those charges was posted, that day counting as day zero, to the same handling date. Where no service charge stands assessed on the account over those months and a payment has been posted to the account over the 12 statement months before the handling date, the overdue days are counted from the day the most recent of those payments was posted, that day counting as day zero, to the same handling date. In every other case the overdue days are counted from no substituted day on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts.

| Service charges standing over the 10 statement months | Payments posted over the 12 statement months | The day the overdue clock starts from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one or more | any | The day the most recent of those charges was posted, counting as day zero, running to the handling date |
| none | one or more | The day the most recent of those payments was posted, counting as day zero, running to the handling date |
| none | none | No substituted day |

Where a charge stands inside its window the most recent charge governs whatever payments stand on the account, the two conditions being read in that order. The day the clock starts from is day zero in either case and the count runs to the handling date, so a charge posted on the 4th of a month and a handling date on the 20th of that month give 16 overdue days.
